text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000074 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation across every complexity tier, but the few charts returned so far support the billed levels, so documentation is too thin to call the pattern either way.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevation is not limited to sicker patients. The 99215 share runs roughly two to four times the all-provider rate in every condition-count tier, including patients with zero or one chronic condition. The sampled low-complexity 99215s include routine-looking encounters such as follow-ups (C0039322, C0039340), upper respiratory infection (C0038762) and UTI (C0038754), which is the pattern that would be consistent with upcoding. Against that, only 2 documented 99215 claims came back, and both supported high MDM. One of them, C0039124, is a one-condition patient, which shows that some low-complexity 99215s can be legitimate, and the code's rule check confirms this is far too few to judge. The 6 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence that notes may be templated or inflated, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and check those notes for cloned language. Separately, the four-condition tier, where the gap to peers is largest, should be checked to see whether the documented MDM there reflects real acuity."}
